title: DPD pilot ALPR Program Documents

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: DPD pilot ALPR Program Documents
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Denver Police Department installed an LPR system as a pilot program at the intersection of 6th and Federal on Oct 19, 2018. It was reported to cost ~$62,000.
In communicating with DPD, I was informed the system’s camera units were Federal Signal, then bought by 3M, then bought by Neology. I am not sure if any of those brands were the vendor.

- Facebook post by DPD, saying "we just added a stationary system at 6th Avenue and Federal Boulevard. We began employing this LPR on October 19th, 2018." 
(https://www.facebook.com/denverpolice/posts/1640540512717592/)
- Article by The Denver Post which mentions "The new installation on Federal cost $62,000" listing their source as "police spokesperson Christine Downs."
(https://www.denverpost.com/2018/10/09/denver-police-license-plate-camera-scan-federal-boulevard/)
- Article from Denver7 which quotes Division Chief (at the time) Ron Thomas: "'That’s a location that we’ve identified through data. We’ve got a lot of stolen vehicles in that area. We’ve had a lot of hit-and-runs at that particular intersection so our data just suggested that would be the best location,' said Division Chief Ron Thomas."
(https://www.denver7.com/news/local-news/denver-police-will-scan-every-license-plate-at-federal-blvd-and-6th-ave)

I filed records request with Denver Department of Safety and they referred me to the Office of the Clerk and Recorder for the records, claiming C&R is the official custodian of the records.

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

- A list of DPD's contracts and receipts from Jan 1, 2017 - Dec 31st, 2018 for cameras, digital recording equipment and image recognition software.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Beckett

title: Flock Safety ALPR Records (Contracts, Audit Logs, SB 34, Communications)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I request the following records concerning any products, services, platforms, sensors, or data feeds of the following categories, whether currently used, previously used, piloted, trialed, or formally considered by this agency, for the period January 1, 2020 through August 19, 2026:

Automated license plate reader ("ALPR") and connected-camera systems — including but not limited to Flock Safety (Flock Group Inc.), Motorola Solutions / Vigilant Solutions (LEARN, PlateSearch), Genetec (AutoVu), Axon / Fusus, Rekor, Leonardo/ELSAG, Neology, and Digital Recognition Network (DRN);
Data-integration, analytics, and "real-time crime center" (RTCC) / "real-time awareness center" (RTAC) platforms — including but not limited to Peregrine Technologies (peregrine.io), Palantir, Fusus (Axon), SoundThinking, and any comparable platform that aggregates, links, or searches across agency data sources; and
Any product beyond ALPR cameras offered by the above vendors (e.g., Flock's Condor PTZ video, FlockOS, Nova, or other data-intelligence products; Peregrine's data-integration or AI/"safety flagging" modules).

Where a term below refers to a Flock-specific feature (e.g., "Organization Audit"), please read it to also request the equivalent record in any other vendor's system.
1. Contracts and procurement. All contracts, master services agreements, order forms, amendments, renewals, statements of work, quotes, proposals, purchase orders, invoices, and payment records with any vendor identified above, including any data-processing addenda / data-processing agreements (DPAs), memoranda of understanding (MOUs), and any competitive-bid waivers or sole-source justifications.
2. Vendor communications. All communications (email, text/SMS, letters, meeting notes, calendar invitations) between agency personnel and representatives of any vendor identified above (including the vendor's @flocksafety.com, @peregrine.io, or equivalent domains), concerning procurement, deployment, configuration, camera or sensor siting, pilot / early-access / free-trial programs, and any product beyond ALPR cameras.
3. Search and audit logs. The complete audit/usage logs showing each search or query, including — for Flock — the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs (Flock Insights dashboard), and — for any RTCC / data-integration platform (e.g., Peregrine) — the user access and query logs. For each entry, please include all available metadata fields, e.g.: record ID, user name, organization/agency name, date/time of search, license plate or query terms, stated reason, case number, camera count, time frame searched, filters, search type, and any text/AI prompt. Please export in the system's native machine-readable format (CSV/XLSX), not as a PDF printout, and do not strip metadata fields.
4. Hotlist and NCIC configuration (commonly the most important item). Records sufficient to show the full hotlist configuration of any ALPR system, including a screenshot, screen capture, printout, or CSV of the hotlists the agency subscribes to. This specifically includes which FBI NCIC "topics" are enabled and, in particular, whether the "Immigration Violator" file / topic is enabled, and the date any such topic was enabled or disabled. Also include any custom hotlists created by the agency.
5. Data sharing and external / federal access. A list of all external entities with which data is shared or from which it is received, and the settings governing that sharing, including:

The agency's Flock network-sharing settings, and whether "National Lookup" and/or statewide lookup are enabled, with the dates access was granted, modified, or revoked;
All external agencies that can access this agency's data, and all agencies whose data this agency can access, with dates;
Specifically, any access by or sharing with federal agencies — ICE, CBP, HSI, ATF, FBI, DHS — including records of searches those agencies (or other agencies on their behalf) ran against this agency's data;
All MOUs, data-sharing agreements, and network-participation terms (e.g., with a fusion center such as NCRIC), and any restrictions placed on downstream use or re-dissemination.

6. California ALPR statutory records (SB 34 and amendments).

The record of access required by Civil Code § 1798.90.52;
The agency's current ALPR usage and privacy policy required by Civil Code § 1798.90.51 (and, if the agency is an ALPR end-user, its policy under § 1798.90.53);
The results of the annual audit of ALPR searches for compliance with the usage/privacy policy (Civil Code § 1798.90.53), including any assessment of whether non-hotlist data was purged within 30 days of collection;
Any records concerning use of ALPR for immigration-enforcement geolocation or retention beyond 30 days (see Civ. Code § 1798.90.5 et seq., as amended).

7. Camera / sensor deployment and locations. Records sufficient to show the number, type, and locations of all cameras or sensors installed in the jurisdiction (fixed ALPR, mobile ALPR, PTZ/video, gunshot-detection, or other), their installation dates, and any encroachment, right-of-way, or other permits issued for their installation.
8. Data sources integrated into any data-integration / RTCC platform. For any platform identified above (e.g., Peregrine), a list of all data sources, feeds, and databases integrated into or accessible through the platform — for example computer-aided dispatch (CAD), records management systems (RMS), body-worn and in-car camera footage, fixed/traffic/school cameras, ALPR data, jail/booking data, DMV or state databases, and any third-party or commercial data sources — together with any system-configuration or data-source inventory documents.
9. Retention, governance, and training. Records reflecting data-retention periods and deletion practices, access controls (who is authorized to search and what approvals are required), prohibited uses, training materials, and internal policies, standard operating procedures, directives, or general orders governing use of any system identified above.
10. Misuse, breaches, and oversight. Any audits, reports, internal-affairs records, complaints, disciplinary records, or communications concerning suspected or confirmed misuse of any system (including searches for personal, immigration, or reproductive-health-related reasons), and any records of data breaches or security incidents involving the data.
11. Surveillance-use policy and impact reports. Any Surveillance Use Policy, Surveillance Impact Report, Privacy Impact Assessment / Data Protection Impact Assessment, or comparable document required by any applicable local surveillance-oversight ordinance, relating to ALPR, RTCC, or data-integration technology generally or to a specific vendor.
12. Governing-body review. Staff reports, resolutions, meeting agendas, minutes, and presentations to the city council / board of supervisors / oversight body concerning approval, funding, or renewal of any contract identified above.
13. Confirmation of non-use. If the agency has never used, piloted, or contracted for any ALPR, connected-camera, RTCC, or data-integration system of the kind described above, please confirm that in writing.

Format, preservation, and processing

Machine-readable format. Please provide records in their original electronic, machine-readable format with metadata intact (Gov. Code § 7922.570); spreadsheets and logs as CSV/XLSX, not PDF printouts.
Preservation. Because some responsive records (particularly ALPR search/audit logs) may be subject to short retention or automatic deletion, I request that the agency preserve all responsive records — and suspend any automatic purge of responsive audit logs — pending completion of this request.
Segregability and exemption log. If any record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify each record and the specific exemption claimed (Gov. Code § 7922.540), and release all reasonably segregable portions (Gov. Code § 7922.525). Data describing how the system operates and is used — as distinct from information about a specific individual — is generally not exempt investigative material (see ACLU of S. Cal. v. Superior Court (2017) 3 Cal.5th 1032). Personal information may be redacted while still disclosing system-level records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Christian Whitney

title: OTH-B (AN/FPS-118) radar: 776th Radar Squadron and program histories with annexes, 1970-1997

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: OTH-B (AN/FPS-118) radar: 776th Radar Squadron and program histories with annexes, 1970-1997
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request the following existing records in the Agency's possession concerning the AN/FPS-118 Over-the-Horizon Backscatter (OTH-B) radar program, covering the period January 1, 1970 through December 31, 1997:

1. Unit histories, including attachments, annexes, and supporting documents, for the 776th Radar Squadron for its OTH-B period, October 1, 1985 through its inactivation on September 6, 1991 (operations center at Bangor Air National Guard Base, Maine; transmit site at Moscow Air Force Station, Maine; receive site at Columbia Falls Air Force Station, Maine);

2. Unit histories, including attachments, annexes, and supporting documents, for the unit or units assigned to operate the West Coast AN/FPS-118 system (operations center at Mountain Home Air Force Base, Idaho; transmit site near Christmas Valley, Oregon; receive site near Tulelake, California), including any numbered squadron, detachment, or operating location so assigned, circa 1985 through the system's placement in caretaker status;

3. The sections and annexes covering the AN/FPS-118 or OTH-B program in the histories of the Electronic Systems Division (later Electronic Systems Center), Hanscom AFB, Massachusetts, and of the Rome Air Development Center, Griffiss AFB, New York, including the 1970-1982 experimental prototype at Moscow and Columbia Falls, Maine, full-scale development under the 1982 GE Aerospace contract, and operational test and evaluation of the East and West Coast systems;

4. Histories or annexes documenting the East Coast system's redirection to counter-narcotics surveillance and continued operation between the 776th Radar Squadron's 1991 inactivation and the cessation of radar operations in October 1997, including any histories of the Northeast Air Defense Sector, Tactical Air Command, or Air Combat Command covering that mission.

This request does not seek published lineage-and-honors statements; publicly available monographs such as "Searching the Skies: The Legacy of the United States Cold War Defense Radar Program" (1997); the Air Combat Command public fact sheet on the OTH-B East and West systems; GAO reports on the OTH-B program; Historic American Engineering Record documentation held by the Library of Congress; or technical reports publicly available through the Defense Technical Information Center (including ADA266949, "Construction and Operation of the West Coast OTH-B Radar System," and ADA333470, "The AN/FPS-118 OTH Radar"). I prefer electronic delivery. Please notify me in advance if any copying or production fees will exceed $50.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robin Monks

title: Historical Investigative Records / Cross-Shared New York State Police Intelligence

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TARGET SUBJECT: Stefano Magaddino (Date of Birth: October 14, 1891 | Date of Death: July 19, 1974)
LOCATION OF RECORDS: FBI Headquarters & FBI Buffalo Field Office

To Whom It May Concern,

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552). 

I am requesting copies of all historical investigative files, intelligence briefs, memos, and indexed records maintained by the FBI Headquarters and the Buffalo Field Office concerning Stefano Magaddino, specifically covering the timeframe of 1957 through 1970.

I specifically request the inclusion of all cross-shared intelligence, logs, transcripts, translations, and summaries provided to the FBI by the New York State Police Bureau of Criminal Investigation (BCI) / "Forest Avenue" undercover squad in Buffalo, New York working as an intelligence unit for the New York State Police. The "Forest Avenue Boys" were the NYSP department's precursor to their New York State Police Organized Crime Task Force. 

Because the subject, Stefano Magaddino, passed away in 1974, individual privacy exemptions under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(7)(C) no longer apply. 

In addition to conducting this search for records at the FBI Field Office in Buffalo, NY, please conduct an additional search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies at FBI Headquarters. 

Please also conduct a search for records at the Alexandria Records Center.

If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records.

If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

FEE WAIVER REQUEST:
I request a waiver of all search and duplication fees because the disclosure of this information is in the public interest. It is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the historical operations of organized crime and mid-century law enforcement coordination in Western New York. These records are strictly for historical research purposes and not for commercial use.

If this request is denied in whole or in part, please justify all deletions by reference to specific exemptions of the Act. Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Mob

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act, 5 ILCS 140/1 et seq., I request copies of records concerning whether Five South Six LLC has been asked, required, agreed, or otherwise discussed paying or reimbursing the Village of La Grange's legal fees and expenses associated with the lawsuit brought by Jonathan Robinson concerning the development at 112 East Burlington Avenue and 5 6th Avenue.

Please provide records from January 1, 2025 through the date of your search responsive to the following:

Communications between the Village and Five South Six LLC, or their respective representatives, concerning payment, reimbursement, indemnification, or defense of the Village's legal fees or expenses relating to the Robinson lawsuit.
Any requests, demands, notices, tenders of defense, agreements, or other records in which the Village asked or required Five South Six LLC to defend, pay, or reimburse the Village for legal fees or litigation expenses.
Any records showing whether Five South Six LLC has agreed, refused, disputed, or otherwise responded to any request that it pay or reimburse the Village's legal expenses.
Invoices, payment records, reimbursement records, or other financial records sufficient to show whether Five South Six LLC has paid or reimbursed any portion of the Village's legal fees or expenses associated with this lawsuit.
Any non-privileged records reflecting a Village determination or discussion concerning whether Sections 11.C or 11.D of the Development Agreement require or permit Five South Six LLC to pay the Village's legal expenses associated with this lawsuit.

For clarity, the contractual provisions prompting this request are Sections 11.C and 11.D of the Development Agreement for 112 East Burlington Avenue and 5 6th Avenue.
